lines.text: The other lane really is faster. You're not imagining it.
You're crawling along, and the next lane just keeps sliding past. It feels like bad luck. Like the universe picked your lane.
But look from above. Slow traffic is packed tight. Fast traffic is spread out.
Drivers leave smaller gaps when they're slow, so a jam squeezes more cars into the same stretch of road.
So at any moment, more drivers are sitting in the slow lane. In this simulation, sixty-two percent of them.
If you feel stuck, the odds say you probably are.
Here's the strange part. Give both lanes exactly the same average speed, and the other one still wins.
Watch this driver. When their lane flows, they zip past the neighbours in a few seconds.
When it jams, they crawl, and the other lane drifts past for a long, long time.
Averaged over every driver, they spend forty-eight percent of the time being overtaken, and only forty-two percent overtaking.
And the cars that pass you stay in view ahead. The ones you pass vanish behind you.
So the other lane isn't magic. Traffic just makes every lane feel like the slow one.
